stem: Who contributed the most to the development of the Bhagavata sect?
expl: The Bhagavata or Vaishnava religion reached its peak during the reign of the Gupta kings. The Gupta rulers were followers of Vaishnavism and probably adopted it as their state religion. Most rulers assumed the title “Paramabhagavata”. Garuda, the vehicle of Vishnu, was the royal emblem of the Guptas.

stem: Nathpanthis, Siddhas and Yogis made devotional religion popular in
expl: The Nathpanthis, Siddhas and Yogis popularized the Bhakti religion in North India. Using simple reasoning and argument, they criticized the ritualistic practices of orthodox religion, other artificial aspects, and the social system of that time. They supported renunciation of the world. According to them, contemplation of the formless Supreme Truth and the experience of becoming one with it is the path to liberation. For this, they emphasized the need to give rigorous training to the mind and body through practices such as yogic postures, pranayama, and contemplation/meditation.

stem: By whom was the first republic of the world was established in Vaishali –
expl: In the 6th century BCE, the world’s first republican system existed at Vaishali. In fact, while monarchies prevailed among the Mahajanapadas in the 6th century, republican governance was prevalent in two states—Vajji and Malla. Vajji was a confederation of eight states, in which the Licchavi of Vaishali were the most powerful.

stem: Which one was the capital of Magadha?
expl: According to the Puranas, the first dynasty to rule Magadha was the Brihadratha dynasty. Jarasandha, the son of Brihadratha (the first king of this dynasty), made Rajgriha (Girivraja) his capital. According to Buddhist texts, the first powerful ruler of Magadha was Bimbisara, who belonged to the Haryanka dynasty. He died in 492 BCE, after which Ajatashatru became the ruler of Magadha. Udayin, the son of Ajatashatru, shifted the capital from Rajgriha to Pataliputra.

stem: What was the name of the dynasty of Ajatashatru?
expl: Ajatashatru (492–460 BCE), the ruler of Magadha, ascended the throne after killing his father Bimbisara, the founder of the Haryanka dynasty. He too was killed by his son Udayin (different from Udayana, the Vatsa king of Kaushambi).

stem: The list of sixteen Mahajanapadas is available in –
expl: In the Buddhist text Anguttara Nikaya, a list of 16 Mahajanapadas is available. These are: (1) Anga, (2) Magadha, (3) Kashi, (4) Kosala, (5) Vajji, (6) Malla, (7) Chedi, (8) Vatsa, (9) Kuru, (10) Panchala, (11) Matsya, (12) Shurasena, (13) Ashmaka, (14) Avanti, (15) Gandhara, and (16) Kamboja. Among these, only Ashmaka was located in South India. In the Buddhist text Digha Nikaya, only 12 Mahajanapadas are mentioned. The Jain text Bhagavati Sutra also gives a list of 16 Mahajanapadas, but the names differ slightly there.

stem: Which dynasty did ruled over Magadha after the Nanda Dynasty?
expl: The Nanda dynasty in Magadha was established after ending the Shishunaga dynasty. There were a total of 9 kings in the Nanda dynasty. In the later period of the Nandas, the people turned against the rulers due to forcible collection of money and heavy taxes even on small items, and an atmosphere of hatred and discontent spread everywhere. Taking advantage of this situation, Chandragupta Maurya, with the help of Chanakya, killed Dhanananda and ended the Nanda dynasty. Thus, immediately after the Nandas, the Maurya dynasty was established in Magadha. After that, the Shungas, Kanvas, Guptas, etc. ruled. Therefore, as per the question, the nearest correct answer is option (a).

stem: King Kharavela is related to –
expl: The Chedi ruler of Kalinga, Kharavela, was one of the greatest emperors of ancient Indian history. An undated inscription of him has been found from the “Hathigumpha” cave on the Udayagiri hill in Bhubaneswar, Odisha. It gives a chronological account of events from Kharavela’s childhood, education, coronation, and the events of the first thirteen years of his reign. This inscription is the main source for knowing Kharavela’s history.

stem: The capital of Anga Janapada was-
expl: The present districts of Bhagalpur and Munger in southern Bihar were included in the Anga Mahajanapada. Its capital was Champa. In the Mahabharata and the Puranas, the ancient name of Champa is found as Malini. According to the Digha Nikaya, the plan for building this city was prepared by the architect Mahagovinda.
